item.title: PowerShell Core: Using Windows-Specific Cmdlets
item.description:
“PowerShell Core: Using Windows-Specific Cmdlets”

When migrating to PowerShell (Core) 7 and beyond, you might encounter situations where certain cmdlets familiar from Windows PowerShell (5.1) are unavailable. This can be a stumbling block, especially when tasks involve interacting with system components like installed software. How can you effectively query installed products in PowerShell Core when the traditional Get-WmiObject cmdlets are absent?

The core of the issue lies in the evolution of PowerShell. While Windows PowerShell 5.1 relies heavily on Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) via Get-WmiObject, PowerShell (Core) 7 has shifted towards a more modern and cross-platform approach using Common Information Model (CIM) cmdlets. Future development for PowerShell is focused on the Core version, making CIM the recommended path forward.
